root.label: Medieval England
root.gloss: How military conquest, feudal control, religious conflict, royal charters, and plague shaped power in England from 1066 to 1485.

children.label: Part 1: Norman Conquest
children.gloss: The 1066 succession crisis, Battle of Hastings, castle building, Harrying of the North, and the 1086 Domesday Book.

children.label: 1. 1066 & Battle of Hastings
children.q2Chain: Succession Crisis & Three Rivals → Stamford Bridge & Forced March → Senlac Shield Wall & Retreat
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Succession Crisis & Three Rivals → Stamford Bridge & Forced March → Senlac Shield Wall & Retreat.

children.label: Succession Crisis & Three Rivals
children.gloss: Edward the Confessor died childless in January 1066, triggering a three-way contest between Harold Godwinson, Duke William, and Harald Hardrada.

children.label: Confessor Died Without Direct Heir
children.gloss: Died childless 5 January 1066; Ended royal House of Wessex.

children.label: Witan Elected Harold Godwinson
children.gloss: Crowned within twenty-four hours; Wealthiest nobleman Earl of Wessex.

children.label: William & Hardrada Staked Claims
children.gloss: William claimed 1051 throne promise; Pope Alexander II blessed banner.

children.label: → Forced Two-Front 1066 Invasion
children.gloss: 300 Viking longships hit Yorkshire; Norman fleet massed across Channel.

children.label: Stamford Bridge & Forced March
children.gloss: Harold marched 190 miles north in four days to crush Hardrada at Stamford Bridge, but weakened his elite troops before marching south.

children.label: 190-Mile March in Four Days
children.gloss: Surprised Vikings on 25 September; Arrow killed King Harald Hardrada.

children.label: 24 Longships Carried Survivors
children.gloss: Shattered Norwegian invasion threat; Showed rapid Saxon mobilisation.

children.label: → Depleted Housecarls Before South
children.gloss: William landed at Pevensey Bay; Forced 250-mile march back south.

children.label: Senlac Shield Wall & Retreat
children.gloss: After five hours holding Senlac Hill, Saxon fyrd militia chased Norman feigned retreats downhill, fracturing the shield wall.

children.label: Five-Hour Senlac Shield Wall
children.gloss: Housecarls swung two-handed axes; Repelled uphill Norman cavalry.

children.label: William Ordered Feigned Retreats
children.gloss: Turned Breton flank panic around; Lured Saxon fyrdmen off ridge.

children.label: → Broke Shield Wall & Slew Harold
children.gloss: Archers angled arrows from above; Crowned William Christmas Day 1066.

children.label: Ended Anglo-Saxon Royal Rule
children.gloss: 10,000 Normans ruled two million; Triggered castle and land seizure.

children.label: 2. Castles, Terror & Domesday
children.q2Chain: Motte-and-Bailey & Stone Keeps → Harrying of the North → Domesday Book & Feudal Pyramid
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Motte-and-Bailey & Stone Keeps → Harrying of the North → Domesday Book & Feudal Pyramid.

children.label: Motte-and-Bailey & Stone Keeps
children.gloss: Normans erected over 500 timber motte-and-bailey castles in days before building towering limestone keeps like Portchester.

children.label: 10,000 Normans vs Two Million
children.gloss: Tiny elite faced hostile Saxons; Needed rapid military strongholds.

children.label: 500 Motte-and-Bailey Castles
children.gloss: Built in eight to fourteen days; Used forced Anglo-Saxon labour.

children.label: Built in eight to fourteen days
children.gloss: Built in eight to fourteen days

children.label: → Replaced Timber with Stone Keeps
children.gloss: Four-storey keep inside Roman walls; Guarded Portsmouth Harbour links.

children.label: Harrying of the North
children.gloss: After rebels slaughtered the Norman garrison at York, William unleashed scorched-earth terror across Yorkshire.

children.label: 1069 York Garrison Slaughtered
children.gloss: Northern rebels backed Danish fleet; Threatened Norman grip on north.

children.label: Scorched-Earth Yorkshire Campaign
children.gloss: Burned crops and killed livestock; Salted fields and smashed ploughs.

children.label: → Starved Over 100,000 People
children.gloss: Chronicled by Orderic Vitalis; Crushed northern revolt forever.

children.label: Domesday Book & Feudal Pyramid
children.gloss: Commissioned in 1085 against Viking invasion fears, the 1086 Domesday Book recorded taxes and sealed Anglo-Saxon dispossession.

children.label: 1085 Danish Invasion Threat
children.gloss: Feared King Cnut IV of Denmark; Ordered Gloucester shire audit.

children.label: Feared King Cnut IV of Denmark
children.gloss: Feared King Cnut IV of Denmark

children.label: Counted Every Shire, Mill & Pig
children.gloss: Royal commissioners took oaths; Secured maximum Crown tax revenue.

children.label: → 200 Barons Held English Land
children.gloss: Over 90% of Saxon land seized; Dispossessed English thegn class.

children.label: Locked Realm in Feudal Pyramid
children.gloss: King leased manors for knights; Bound peasantry in serfdom.

children.label: Part 2: Crown, Church & Law
children.gloss: The bloody clash between Henry II and Thomas Becket over Church courts, and the baronial rebellion forcing King John to seal Magna Carta.

children.label: 3. Henry II & Thomas Becket
children.q2Chain: Appointment & Spiritual Shift → Constitutions of Clarendon → Cathedral Murder & 1174 Penance
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Appointment & Spiritual Shift → Constitutions of Clarendon → Cathedral Murder & 1174 Penance.

children.label: Appointment & Spiritual Shift
children.gloss: Henry II appointed his worldly Chancellor Thomas Becket Archbishop in 1162, but Becket became an austere defender of the Pope.

children.label: Henry Sought Pliable Church Ally
children.gloss: Appointed hunting friend in 1162; Hoped to control Church wealth.

children.label: Becket Donned Lice Hairshirt
children.gloss: Resigned royal Chancellorship; Washed thirteen paupers daily.

children.label: → Put Papal Loyalty Above Crown
children.gloss: Defended independent Church law; Set collision course with Henry.

children.label: Constitutions of Clarendon
children.gloss: Henry II issued the 1164 Constitutions of Clarendon to try criminous clerks in royal courts, driving Becket into French exile.

children.label: Scandal of Criminous Clerks
children.gloss: Clergy read Latin psalm verse; Escaped royal gallows for murder.

children.label: 1164 Clarendon Court Demands
children.gloss: Demanded royal trials for priests; Becket refused to seal document.

children.label: → Six-Year French Exile & Rift
children.gloss: Fled secretly across Channel; Excommunicated royalist bishops.

children.label: Cathedral Murder & 1174 Penance
children.gloss: Four knights murdered Becket in Canterbury Cathedral in December 1170, forcing Henry II into barefoot penance and compromise.

children.label: Henry Shouted Furious Outburst
children.gloss: Raged against miserable drones; Four knights crossed icy Channel.

children.label: Slain Before Canterbury Altar
children.gloss: Murdered 29 December 1170 dusk; Canonised by Pope Alexander III.

children.label: → 1174 Barefoot Whipping Penance
children.gloss: Flogged by eighty Canterbury monks; Dropped Clarendon court clauses.

children.label: Protected Church Courts for Ages
children.gloss: Miracles drew medieval pilgrims; Clerical immunity lasted to Tudors.

children.label: 4. King John & Magna Carta
children.q2Chain: Normandy Loss & Papal Interdict → Bouvines & Baronial Rebellion → Runnymede & First Barons’ War
children.gloss: Causal Chain: Normandy Loss & Papal Interdict → Bouvines & Baronial Rebellion → Runnymede & First Barons’ War.

children.label: Normandy Loss & Papal Interdict
children.gloss: Losing Normandy in 1204 and feuding with Pope Innocent III left England under a five-year Interdict and heavy royal extortion.

children.label: 1204 Loss of Ancestral Normandy
children.gloss: Defeated by Philip II of France; Mocked as John Softsword.

children.label: Defeated by Philip II of France
children.gloss: Defeated by Philip II of France

children.label: 1208 Five-Year Papal Interdict
children.gloss: Rejected Stephen Langton choice; Seized £100,000 church revenues.

children.label: → 1213 Surrender as Papal Fief
children.gloss: Churches locked; dead unhallowed; Paid Pope 1,000 marks yearly.

children.label: Bouvines & Baronial Rebellion
children.gloss: Crushed at Bouvines in July 1214, bankrupt King John faced armed barons who seized London in May 1215.

children.label: July 1214 Bouvines Defeat
children.gloss: French smashed mercenary allies; Ended Normandy reconquest dream.

children.label: Scutage Revolt & London Seized
children.gloss: Fitzwalter led Army of God; Captured London in May 1215.

children.label: → Forced Runnymede Peace Talks
children.gloss: Royal treasury stood bankrupt; Cornered John beside Thames.

children.label: Runnymede & First Barons’ War
children.gloss: On 15 June 1215 John sealed Magna Carta’s 63 clauses including Clause 39, though papal annulment sparked civil war.

children.label: 63 Clauses Sealed 15 June 1215
children.gloss: Curbed arbitrary scutage taxes; Protected baronial heirs and widows.

children.label: Clause 39 Lawful Peer Judgment
children.gloss: Barred unlawful free-man prison; Placed English king beneath law.

children.label: → Papal Annulment & Barons’ War
children.gloss: Prince Louis marched into London; Crown jewels lost in the Wash.

children.label: Crown jewels lost in the Wash
children.gloss: Crown jewels lost in the Wash

children.label: Liberty Bedrock vs Baron Grab
children.gloss: Served elite barons in 1215; William Marshal reissued for 9yo.

children.label: Part 3: Plague & Revolt
children.gloss: The 1348 Black Death killed nearly half the population, triggering wage laws, regressive Poll Taxes, and the 1381 Peasants’ Revolt.

children.label: 5. Black Death & Peasants’ Revolt
children.q2Chain: 1348 Plague & Labour Shortage → 1351 Wage Freeze & Poll Taxes → Smithfield & End of Serfdom
children.gloss: Causal Chain: 1348 Plague & Labour Shortage → 1351 Wage Freeze & Poll Taxes → Smithfield & End of Serfdom.

children.label: 1348 Plague & Labour Shortage
children.gloss: Arriving at Melcombe Regis in June 1348, bubonic plague killed nearly half of England and gave surviving workers bargaining power.

children.label: June 1348 Melcombe Regis Arrival
children.gloss: Gascony ship carried plague fleas; Killed nearly half the country.

children.label: → Severe Rural Worker Shortage
children.gloss: Crops rotted in empty fields; Workers demanded double wages.

children.label: Cracked Customary Manorial Grip
children.gloss: Serfs left manors for cash pay; Shifted rural bargaining power.

children.label: Serfs left manors for cash pay
children.gloss: Serfs left manors for cash pay

children.label: 1351 Wage Freeze & Poll Taxes
children.gloss: Parliament froze wages in 1351 and levied flat 12d Poll Taxes for war, sparking the May 1381 Brentwood uprising.

children.label: 1351 Statute of Labourers Cap
children.gloss: Froze wages at pre-plague pay; Branded runaway serfs with F.

children.label: 1363 Dress Ban & 1381 Poll Tax
children.gloss: Banned peasants wearing fine fur; Flat 12d tax funded French war.

children.label: → May 1381 Brentwood Insurrection
children.gloss: Villagers chased out John Bampton; Ignited Essex and Kent revolt.

children.label: Smithfield & End of Serfdom
children.gloss: Wat Tyler and John Ball led 30,000 rebels into London; despite Tyler’s death at Smithfield, Poll Taxes ended and serfdom withered.

children.label: 30,000 Rebels Stormed London
children.gloss: Wat Tyler and John Ball led; Burned tax rolls; took Tower.

children.label: Wat Tyler and John Ball led
children.gloss: Wat Tyler and John Ball led

children.label: 15 June Smithfield Confrontation
children.gloss: 14-year-old Richard II promised; London Mayor stabbed Wat Tyler.

children.label: → Revolt Crushed; Poll Tax Ended
children.gloss: Boy king revoked freedom charters; Parliament dropped flat Poll Tax.

children.label: Feudal Serfdom Withered Away
children.gloss: Landlords hired free wage hands; Ended medieval English bondage.
